events.title: The Battle of Hastings
events.description: Duke William of Normandy's army defeated King Harold II's English forces near Hastings. Harold was killed in the fighting.
events.significance: The victory began the Norman conquest of England. It reshaped the country's monarchy, language, law and culture for centuries.

events.title: Theodore Roosevelt Shot Before a Speech
events.description: While campaigning for president in Milwaukee, Theodore Roosevelt was shot in the chest by a would-be assassin. His speech text and glasses case slowed the bullet. He went ahead and spoke for about an hour before he went to hospital.
events.significance: The episode became a famous example of political toughness. It came during his Progressive Party run in the 1912 election.

events.title: Chuck Yeager Breaks the Sound Barrier
events.description: U.S. Air Force Captain Chuck Yeager flew the experimental Bell X-1 faster than the speed of sound over the Mojave Desert in California.
events.significance: The flight showed that humans could fly faster than sound. It opened the way for supersonic aviation and the early space age.

events.title: Martin Luther King Jr. Wins the Nobel Peace Prize
events.description: Martin Luther King Jr. was announced as the winner of the Nobel Peace Prize. At 35, he was the youngest recipient to that point. He was honored for leading nonviolent resistance to racial inequality in the United States.
events.significance: The prize brought international recognition to the American civil rights movement. It strengthened its moral standing as major civil rights legislation took shape.
